title: Clark-West Tests on Equity Premium Forecasts
text: recursive (expanding-window) loop used every predictor. forecast date t+1t+1, historical-mean benchmark uses y‾1:t\bar y_{1:t}; alternative regresses y2:ty_{2:t} x1:(t−1)x_{1:(t-1)} forecasts using xtx_t.
code: recursive_forecasts <- function(y, x, R) {   T_ <- length(y)   P  <- T_ - R   e1 <- e2 <- f1 <- f2 <- numeric(P)    for (j in seq_len(P)) {     # estimation sample: rows 1..(R+j-1); forecast target: row R+j     train_y <- y[1:(R + j - 1)]     train_x <- x[1:(R + j - 1)]      # benchmark: prevailing mean of y observed up to t     f1[j] <- mean(train_y)      # alternative: y_t = a + b * x_{t-1} + e     fit <- lm(yt ~ xlag, data = data.frame(       yt   = train_y[-1],       xlag = train_x[-length(train_x)]     ))     f2[j] <- as.numeric(stats::predict(       fit, newdata = data.frame(xlag = train_x[length(train_x)])     ))      e1[j] <- y[R + j] - f1[j]     e2[j] <- y[R + j] - f2[j]   }    list(e1 = e1, e2 = e2, f1 = f1, f2 = f2, P = P) }

title: Clark-West Tests on Equity Premium Forecasts
text: use first 241 monthly observations (1926-12 1946-12) initial estimation window evaluate next 768 months (1947-01 2010-12). Clark-West test, macro predictors vs. historical mean (rz2013) positive R2OS_pct indicates alternative model lower --sample MSFE historical-mean benchmark; Clark-West t-statistic compared one-sided standard normal H0:ROS2≤0H_0:\, \text{R}^2_{OS} \le 0.
code: y_rz   <- rz2013$eq_prem preds_rz <- setdiff(names(rz2013), c("date", "eq_prem")) R_rz   <- 241L  cw_rz <- lapply(preds_rz, function(p) {   fc <- recursive_forecasts(y_rz, rz2013[[p]], R = R_rz)   res <- cw_test(fc$e1, fc$e2, fc$f1, fc$f2)   data.frame(     predictor = p,     R2OS_pct  = unname(res$r2os),     CW_stat   = unname(res$statistic),     p_value   = unname(res$pvalue)   ) }) cw_rz <- do.call(rbind, cw_rz) cw_rz <- cw_rz[order(-cw_rz$CW_stat), ]  knitr::kable(cw_rz, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,              caption = "Clark-West test, macro predictors vs. historical mean (rz2013)")

title: Clark-West Tests on Equity Premium Forecasts
text: technical indicators binary signals constructed S&P 500 prices volume. use first 181 observations (1950-12 1965-12) initial estimation window evaluate next 552 months (1966-01 2011-12), matching paper. Clark-West test, technical indicators vs. historical mean (nrtz2014) technical indicators deliver positive R²OS Clark-West statistics significant conventional levels, consistent headline finding Neely et al. (2014): simple price-based volume-based signals contain economically meaningful information equity premium.
code: y_nr   <- nrtz2014$eq_prem preds_nr <- setdiff(names(nrtz2014), c("date", "eq_prem")) R_nr   <- 181L  cw_nr <- lapply(preds_nr, function(p) {   fc <- recursive_forecasts(y_nr, nrtz2014[[p]], R = R_nr)   res <- cw_test(fc$e1, fc$e2, fc$f1, fc$f2)   data.frame(     predictor = p,     R2OS_pct  = unname(res$r2os),     CW_stat   = unname(res$statistic),     p_value   = unname(res$pvalue)   ) }) cw_nr <- do.call(rbind, cw_nr) cw_nr <- cw_nr[order(-cw_nr$CW_stat), ]  knitr::kable(cw_nr, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,              caption = "Clark-West test, technical indicators vs. historical mean (nrtz2014)")

title: Clark-West Tests on Equity Premium Forecasts
text: cumulative squared-error differential (Goyal-Welch, 2008) tracks predictor outperforms historical mean. upward- sloping line means technical indicator better; steep gains tend cluster around recessions, exactly regime documented Neely et al. (2014).
code: fc_ma <- recursive_forecasts(nrtz2014$eq_prem, nrtz2014$MA_2_12, R = R_nr) cw_test(fc_ma$e1, fc_ma$e2, fc_ma$f1, fc_ma$f2) #>  #> ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │               Clark-West Test (2007)               │ #> ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ #> │ H0: Benchmark MSFE <= Alternative MSFE             │ #> │ H1: Alternative model is superior (R2OS > 0)       │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Test Results:                                      │ #> │  CW statistic: 1.6925                              │ #> │  P-value (one-sided): 0.0453                       │ #> │  R2OS (%): 0.78                                    │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Details:                                           │ #> │  Observations (n): 552                             │ #> │  Reference distribution: N(0,1)                    │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ oos_dates <- tail(nrtz2014$date, fc_ma$P) loss_diff <- fc_ma$e1^2 - fc_ma$e2^2  ggplot(data.frame(date = oos_dates, cum = cumsum(loss_diff)),        aes(date, cum)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +   geom_line(colour = "#47A5C5", linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = NULL,        y = "Cumulative SE diff (mean - MA(2,12))",        title = "Cumulative squared-error differential, MA(2,12) vs. historical mean",        subtitle = "Above zero means the technical indicator is winning") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

title: Replicating Rossi (2006), Table 1: Diebold-Mariano Tests
text: Let ete_t denote log exchange rate Δet=et−et−1\Delta e_t = e_t - e_{t-1} monthly return. Two competing one-step-ahead forecasts Δet+1\Delta e_{t+1}: Benchmark – driftless random walk: Δêt+1RW=0\widehat{\Delta e}^{RW}_{t+1} = 0. Alternative – AR(p): Δêt+1AR=α̂t+∑k=1pβ̂k,tΔet−k+1\widehat{\Delta e}^{AR}_{t+1} = \hat\alpha_t + \sum_{k=1}^{p} \hat\beta_{k,t}\, \Delta e_{t-k+1}, coefficients re-estimated period. Following Rossi, AR(1) AR(2) start usable sample nobs=307n_{obs} = 307 returns. first R=⌈nobs/2⌉=154R = \lceil n_{obs}/2 \rceil = 154 used fit initial model remaining P=153P = 153 evaluated sample. Three estimation schemes considered: Split – coefficients estimated 1:R1{:}R held fixed. Recursive – coefficients re-estimated period using available data. Rolling – coefficients re-estimated period using recent RR observations.
code: forecast_oos <- function(log_fx, p, scheme = c("split", "recursive", "rolling")) {   scheme <- match.arg(scheme)    T_full <- length(log_fx)   dy <- diff(log_fx)   Y  <- dy[3:(T_full - 1)]   L1 <- dy[2:(T_full - 2)]   L2 <- dy[1:(T_full - 3)]   Xm <- if (p == 1) matrix(L1, ncol = 1) else cbind(L1, L2)    n_obs <- length(Y)   R     <- as.integer(ceiling(n_obs / 2))   P_oos <- n_obs - R    e_alt   <- numeric(P_oos)   e_bench <- numeric(P_oos)    for (j in seq_len(P_oos)) {     idx <- switch(scheme,       split     = seq_len(R),       recursive = seq_len(R + j - 1),       rolling   = j:(R + j - 1)     )     Z <- cbind(1, Xm[idx, , drop = FALSE])     b <- as.numeric(solve(crossprod(Z), crossprod(Z, Y[idx])))     pred <- as.numeric(c(1, Xm[R + j, ]) %*% b)      e_alt[j]   <- Y[R + j] - pred     e_bench[j] <- Y[R + j]   }    list(e_bench = e_bench, e_alt = e_alt, P = P_oos) }

what: Replicating the OOS DM panel of Table 1
title: Replicating Rossi (2006), Table 1: Diebold-Mariano Tests
text: use dm_test() correction = FALSE match Rossi’s asymptotic χ2(1)\chi^2(1) reference distribution. Rossi defines loss differential ft=utAR−utRWf_t = u^{AR}_t - u^{RW}_t, positive DM statistic means random walk lower MSFE. reproduce sign pass AR errors e1 random-walk errors e2.
code: countries <- levels(rossi2006$country) schemes   <- c("split", "recursive", "rolling")  run_panel <- function(p) {   out <- expand.grid(country = countries, scheme = schemes,                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   out$DM   <- NA_real_   out$DM_p <- NA_real_    for (i in seq_len(nrow(out))) {     log_fx <- log(subset(rossi2006, country == out$country[i])$fx)     fc     <- forecast_oos(log_fx, p = p, scheme = out$scheme[i])     res    <- dm_test(fc$e_alt, fc$e_bench,                       alternative = "two.sided", correction = FALSE)     out$DM[i]   <- res$statistic     out$DM_p[i] <- res$pvalue   }    out$cell <- sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", out$DM, out$DM_p)   wide <- reshape(out[, c("country", "scheme", "cell")],                   idvar = "scheme", timevar = "country", direction = "wide")   names(wide) <- gsub("^cell\\.", "", names(wide))   wide }

code: log_fx_jp <- log(subset(rossi2006, country == "Japan")$fx) fc_jp     <- forecast_oos(log_fx_jp, p = 1, scheme = "recursive")  dm_test(fc_jp$e_alt, fc_jp$e_bench,         alternative = "two.sided", correction = FALSE) #>  #> ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │            Diebold-Mariano Test (1995)             │ #> ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ #> │ H0: Equal predictive ability                       │ #> │ H1: Methods have different predictive ability      │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Test Results:                                      │ #> │  DM statistic: 0.0001                              │ #> │  P-value: 0.9999                                   │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Details:                                           │ #> │  Observations (n): 153                             │ #> │  Forecast horizon (h): 1                           │ #> │  Loss function: SE                                 │ #> │  Reference distribution: N(0,1)                    │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ loss_diff <- fc_jp$e_alt^2 - fc_jp$e_bench^2 oos_dates <- tail(unique(rossi2006$date), fc_jp$P)  ggplot(data.frame(date = oos_dates, cum = cumsum(loss_diff)),        aes(date, cum)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +   geom_line(colour = "#47A5C5", linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = NULL,        y = "Cumulative SE loss (AR(1) - RW)",        title = "Cumulative squared-error loss differential, Japan",        subtitle = "Above zero = RW doing better; below = AR(1) doing better") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

title: Unconditional Superior Predictive Ability (USPA/SPA) Test — spa_test
text: SPA test statistic : $$T^{SPA} = \max_{1 \le j \le J} \frac{\sqrt{n}\, \bar{d}_j}{\hat{\sigma}_j}$$ \(\bar{d}_j\) mean loss differential competitor j \(\hat{\sigma}_j\) estimated standard deviation. null hypothesis rejected benchmark superior competitors, .e., competitor significantly outperforms . Hansen's (2005) consistent test uses pre-selection step remove clearly inferior competitors critical value computation.
